label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Fernhollow Photo is a real business now

Hi everyone!

I have news, and I'm going to be honest that I'm a little bit freaking out while I type this. Fernhollow Photo is official. I filed the LLC, the website is live, and I'm going out on my own as a wedding photographer.

Some of you already know I've been shooting for Rosebud Lane for the last four years. Marisol Vance (no, not the Vance from the Rosebud Lane brochure, the real one who taught me everything) decided to close the studio at the end of October. That's her story to tell, not mine, so I'll just say it was a hard thing to hear and I'm grateful she told me herself, early, and in person-ish. I found out on October 6, and the very next thing she did was start referring her couples to me. Six of the 2027 weddings on my calendar came from her. Marisol, if you're reading this, you are the reason I know how to do any of this, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. Thank you.

The other eight 2027 weddings found me on their own, which still feels a little unreal. So right now I have fourteen weddings booked for next year. My busiest month is going to be June, with four weddings. The furthest out one is a September wedding at Wallowa Lake, which I'm honestly thrilled about because I've wanted an excuse to go back there for years.

Now the part I know some of you are going to worry about, so let me get ahead of it. I'm not doing this recklessly. I've been planning it in my head for about two years. I've been saving, watching the numbers, learning the business side of things, and waiting until I had enough work lined up that I felt like I wasn't gambling on myself. I know that's not the same as saying it isn't scary. It is. I'm scared. But I have a plan, and it's a real one.

Here's what the plan looks like. I have a second shooter, Jae, who has worked with me on the big weddings and gets paid per wedding, so I'm not trying to be in two places at once. And yes, that means I'm hiring someone, which feels very grown up.

Dad, before you ask at Ruthie's: yes, I have health insurance. I picked a marketplace plan, and it starts January 1. You can stop worrying about that one now.

The first wedding that is 100% mine, start to finish, is Dahlia and Ken's, at Timberline on June 12. They found me through the photos from the Multnomah Falls couple I shot for Marisol's studio, and when Dahlia emailed to say they were in, I read it four times in a row in the parking lot. That was the moment it started to feel real.

The day I filed the LLC, I did it on my lunch break, sitting in my car outside a Fred Meyer. I filled out the form, hit submit, and cried a little, and then I went back in and bought a sandwich I didn't taste. Sam says that's the most Tessa thing he's ever heard. He's probably right.

Sam also made a cake to celebrate. It said FERNHOLOW. He spelled it FERNHOLOW, which is one L short. We ate it anyway, and it was delicious, and I will be hearing about that spelling for the rest of my life.

Now, the name. Fernhollow comes from the fern hollow trail behind Grandma's old place in Gresham. That's where I took my first real pictures, with Grandma's old Pentax, which she let me carry around like it was made of glass. I was maybe twelve. Every frame was blurry and about half the fern fronds were cut off, and she told me the good ones would come eventually if I kept walking and kept looking. So Grandma, this one's for you. You should know that before anybody else does. I'm doing this because you handed me a camera and told me to keep looking.

Which brings me to Thanksgiving. Since I'm going to be at Ruthie's anyway, I'm bringing the camera. If anybody wants free family pictures, whether it's just you and your kids, a couple of cousins, or the whole crowd around the turkey, I would love to do it. Consider it my thank you for putting up with me all these years. Mom already knows I'm going to try to get everybody to stop eating long enough for one photo. Good luck to me.

I'm nervous, excited, a little overwhelmed, and mostly really grateful. Thank you for every time you asked how work was going, every time you sent a referral, and every time you hung on to a blurry photo I took and told me it was good. It mattered more than you know.

Love you all. Come find me at Thanksgiving if you want to get your picture taken, or just come find me to say hi.

Tessa
Fernhollow Photo
